title: Overly Broad Observers (The God Listener)
pattern: Defining a single, massive observer/listener trait containing many unrelated callback methods, forcing all implementers to write empty default bodies for events they do not care about.
why_bad: It couples unrelated components to a single bloated interface, violating the Single Responsibility Principle. Implementers of specific tasks are forced to depend on events from entirely separate modules.
detection: A trait containing 3 or more methods representing notifications of unrelated domain events, where concrete implementers commonly leave several methods empty.
counterexample: Unified UI frameworks where a single event listener is structured as an explicit enum pattern to support uniform message passing.
fix: Split the observer into small, cohesive, highly targeted traits (e.g., `UserLifecycleListener`, `PaymentListener`).
source: Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004), Chapter 7 ("Unify Interfaces").
